Fusion cells have their cathodes made from nickel-oxide, and their anodes from palladium. Palladium is used because it can absorb up to nine hundred times its own volume of hydrogen, although, the details of this process are still poorly understood. When the beta active nuclides emit beta particles, they excite their own electrons in the narrow excimer band at a minimum of thermal losses, such that this radiation is converted in a high band gap photovoltaic layer very efficiently into electricity. <end>
